subject: Archaeology
title: Ancient DNA: Decoding the Past
description: A quick, practical guide to Ancient DNA: Decoding the Past.

hook.text: A pinch of dust from a 40,000-year-old bone can reveal who that person was related to — and who they married.

buildup.text: Ancient DNA (aDNA) is extracted from bones, teeth, and even soil. Cold, dry conditions preserve it best.

discovery.text: aDNA proved that modern Europeans are a mix of three ancient populations: hunter-gatherers, farmers, and steppe herders.

twist.text: Contamination is a huge problem. A single sneeze can ruin a sample. Labs require full clean-room suits.

climax.text: aDNA identified the Denisovans — an entirely new human species — from a single finger bone found in a Siberian cave.

punchline.text: One bone, one finger, one new human species.

quiz.question: How were the Denisovans discovered?
options: A complete skeleton was found in a Chinese burial site
DNA from a single finger bone in a Siberian cave identified a new species
Linguistic analysis of ancient texts revealed references to an unknown people

details.summary: Ancient DNA (aDNA) extracted from bones, teeth, and sediments reveals genetic information about past populations — their origins, migrations, diet, diseases, and family relationships.
details.whyItMatters: Ancient DNA provides direct biological evidence about past peoples that no artifact or text can match. It has settled longstanding debates about migrations, interbreeding with Neanderthals, and the spread of farming across Europe.
takeaways: DNA extracted from ancient bones reveals population origins and movements
The field has rewritten major chapters of human migration history
Teeth and dense bones preserve DNA best over millennia

faq.question: What types of samples preserve ancient DNA best?
faq.answer: The petrous bone — the densest bone in the body, located behind the ear — preserves DNA far better than other skeletal elements. Teeth also preserve DNA well. Cold, dry environments favor preservation. DNA degrades rapidly in warm, humid conditions.

faq.question: What has ancient DNA revealed about human history?
faq.answer: It proved humans interbred with Neanderthals and Denisovans. It showed farming spread to Europe partly through migration of Anatolian farmers. It revealed massive Bronze Age steppe migrations into Europe. Each year brings new studies rewriting regional population histories.
